question: How many advance votes will the NZ Electoral Commission report for Thursday 29 October 2026 (daily count, day 4 of advance voting)?

calls.reasoning: 2023 had the same 12-day calendar. Its day-4 (Thursday) figure was 103,617 in the table revised in Feb 2024 to include specials; live ordinary-only figures ran at about 84-89% of revised, implying ~89-92k live on day 4. For 2026: no enrolment during voting removes those specials; enrolment is similar (~3.64M); Labour Day falls on day 1; the 2026 table may show a combined total. Election-to-election swings in advance voting are large (1.24M/1.98M/1.64M). No human market found (the Manifold candidates are about the Orange Guy mascot and irrelevant).
calls.dossier:
- 2023 Electoral Commission daily advance table (revised Feb 2024 to include specials; excludes overseas), elections.nz: Oct 2 65,845; Oct 3 80,899; Oct 4 88,671; Thu Oct 5 (day 4) 103,617; Fri Oct 6 110,674; Sat 154,111; Sun 108,375; Mon 148,476; Tue 147,260; Wed 166,716; Thu 205,341; Fri 260,219; total 1,640,204.
- Live 2023 ordinary-only figures (1News 6 Oct 2023): day 1 58,308 (vs 65,845 revised, ratio 0.886); first three days 204,191 (vs 235,415 revised, ratio 0.867). Wikipedia: 1,376,366 advance votes for 2023 overall (ordinary; ratio about 0.84 of revised total).
- 2020: first 3 days 264,744; day 1 92,434 (NZ Herald/1News); total ~1.98M over 14 days (calendar differs). 2017 total 1.24M.
- 2026: election Sat 7 Nov; advance voting Mon 26 Oct (Labour Day public holiday) to Fri 6 Nov, 12 days, matching the 2023 alignment; ~850 advance voting places (ODT).
- 2026: enrolment closes 25 Oct and there is no enrolment during the voting period (in 2023 ~450k enrolled during the voting period, which generated special votes). ~3.6M enrolled (~89%), 18-24 enrolment low (RNZ/ODT, Oct 2026). The Commission anticipates ~700k special votes overall (ODT).
- Opposition says the election date and the law change limit turnout (RNZ/The Brief, 18 Oct 2026).
- Status quo: a 2023-like pattern; day 4 is about 6.3% of the 12-day advance total.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the daily figure for 29 Oct on the Commission's 2026 voting-statistics page as displayed at resolution; combined ordinary+special if shown, otherwise ordinary only. Retrospective additions are not counted.
- Event window: single day, 29 Oct 2026; as of 19 Oct 2026, 0% elapsed (advance voting not yet started).
- Searched but not found: any 2026 daily advance figures (voting not started); whether the 2026 table will include specials live; the live 2023 day-4 ordinary figure directly; any prediction market.
calls.reference_class: NZ general election advance voting, day-4 daily counts (2023 aligned calendar; 2020/2017 totals for scale)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: day-4 (first Thursday in 2023) daily advance vote counts in recent NZ general elections. 2023 day 4 (Thu 5 Oct) = 103,617 in the retrospectively updated table incl. specials; the live 2023 reports covered only ordinary votes (first 3 days 204,191 live vs 235,415 updated, ~0.87), so the live day-4 figure was ~90k. 2026 has the same 12-day Monday-start schedule. No enrolment during voting means fewer specials but more ordinary voters enrolled in advance. Population growth adds ~3%. Day 1 falls on Labour Day, which barely affects Thursday. Downside risks are concerns about lower youth enrolment/turnout. Upside: possible counting of specials in the table, and the long-run growth of advance voting. Market check: no matching market found (the Manifold candidates are about the Orange Guy mascot, which is irrelevant). Median ~94k.
calls.dossier:
- Elections NZ 2023 voting-statistics page (fetched 2026-10-19): daily advance votes 2023 (retrospectively incl. specials, Feb 2024): Mon 2 Oct 65,845; Tue 80,899; Wed 88,671; Thu 5 Oct 103,617; Fri 110,674; Sat 154,111; Sun 108,375; Mon 9 Oct 148,476; Tue 147,260; Wed 166,716; Thu 205,341; Fri 13 Oct 260,219; total 1,640,204.
- The same table, aligned by calendar date (alignment uncertain): 2020 column (voting began Sat 3 Oct 2020) shows 118,585 on what appears to be day 4; 2017 column shows 72,932 in the same row (2017 day 4 ~ Thursday). Totals: 2017 1,240,740; 2020 1,976,996.
- NZ Herald 2023: first three days of 2023 advance voting reported live = 204,191 (vs 264,744 in 2020's same period). The updated table sums to 235,415 for those days, so the live/ordinary-only figure was ~0.87 of the updated figure. Implied 2023 live day-4 figure ~90k.
- 2023 ordinary advance votes 1,368,830 = 61.0% of ordinary votes (vs 68% in 2020).
- 2026: election Sat 7 Nov; advance voting Mon 26 Oct (Labour Day public holiday) to Fri 6 Nov; ~850 advance voting places (ODT). Enrolment closed 25 Oct, with no enrolment during voting (law change). In 2023 ~450k enrolled during the voting period (many cast special votes).
- Enrolment: ~3.64M enrolled late Sept 2026 (~89.8% of eligible). 18-24 enrolment 65.5% as of 15 Oct (RNZ / The Brief, 18 Oct 2026). Opposition is raising voter-suppression concerns.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the daily figure for 29 Oct on the Commission's 2026 voting-statistics page at resolution time (live figures were ordinary-only in 2023; use the combined figure if specials are shown). Retrospective additions are ignored. Overseas votes are excluded.
- Event window: single day Thu 29 Oct 2026 (day 4); as of 2026-10-19, 0% elapsed, advance voting not yet started.
- No market found on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold for this count.
- Searched for and could not find: 2026 Commission projections of advance-vote volume; the number of 2023 advance voting places for comparison.
calls.reference_class: Daily advance-vote counts on day 4 (first Thursday where applicable) of NZ general elections 2017-2023, Electoral Commission voting-statistics tables

calls.reasoning: Anchor: 2023 day 4 (Thu 5 Oct, same calendar alignment) was 103,617 incl. specials; live ordinary-only was ~87% of that (first three days live 204,191 vs final table 235,415), i.e. ~90k. In 2026 enrolment closes before advance voting, so nearly all votes are ordinary and live counts should be closer to combined totals; offsetting this, some 2023 enrol-and-vote voters drop out and youth enrolment is lower. Labour Day falls on day 1 and may shift timing. Advance-vote totals have swung widely across cycles (1.24M/1.98M/1.64M), hence a wide distribution. No market found (only unrelated Manifold mascot markets).

calls.reference_class: Day-4 (first Thursday) daily advance-vote counts in NZ general elections with 12-day advance periods (2023; 2020/2017 adjusted for alignment)

calls.reasoning: Same 12-day Monday-start calendar as 2023; 2023 day 4 = 103,617 in revised table incl. specials, live ordinary-only ~0.87x => ~90k. 2026: pre-voting enrolment closure shifts some would-be specials to ordinary but Commission still expects many specials and some enrol-and-vote voters drop out; lower youth enrolment offsets population growth. Median ~94k, right skew for possibility of combined figures. No human market exists.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs share identical facts (2023 daily table, ~0.87 live/revised ratio, 2026 calendar alignment, enrolment law change, no market). Disagreement is judgment only: whether 2026 live counts approach combined (Run 3, median 100k) or stay near 2023 ordinary-only (~90-94k, Runs 1-2). The cited ~700k anticipated specials suggests specials persist and live counts stay ordinary-only, so I lean toward Runs 1-2 with modest upside skew. Carried forward the runs' reference class; no web access this run.

disagreements.claim: 2026 live daily figures will be close to combined (ordinary+special) because enrolment closes before voting
disagreements.verdict: Partially rejected: ~700k anticipated specials and post-roll-print enrollees voting special imply live ordinary-only figures remain well below combined; kept as upside skew

disagreements.claim: Net effect of law change/youth enrolment on day-4 volume vs 2023
disagreements.verdict: Roughly offsetting with population growth; no evidence breaks tie; centered near 2023 live level plus small growth
Took ~51k reflecting cross-cycle swings and instrument uncertainty
